4. The parties are present in Court today.
The Petitioners have been identified by their Counsel and the Investigating Officer.
The Respondent No.2/complainant has been identified by her Counsel and the Investigating Officer.

The Complainant/Respondent No.2 states that she has received the entire amount as per the settlement and has settled all her matrimonial disputes with the Petitioners out of her own free will, without pressure, coercion or undue influence and states that she does not want to pursue the present case any further and requests that the present FIR and the proceedings emanating therefrom may be quashed.
The parties undertake that they will remain bound by the settlement and proceedings recorded before this Court.

5. Considering the fact that the dispute is a matrimonial dispute and the parties have amicably settled their disputes, the present case is squarely covered under the law laid down by the Supreme Court in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303.
